blocks.content: 1. FIRST UNDERSTAND THIS — WHY CLAUSES MATTER

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Clauses are fundamental structural units built around complete or incomplete thoughts.
The distinction between Independent (Main) and Dependent (Subordinate) clauses forms the foundation of clause analysis.
The three major clause types tested in competitive exams are Noun Clauses, Adjective Clauses, and Adverb Clauses.
Embedded Noun Clauses require standard statement word order rather than question word order.
Participle and reduced clauses require careful handling to avoid dangling modifiers and sentence errors.
